review_note: Confirmed via the linked continuation order JML 24-48's own text: 'the State of Louisiana experienced extreme drought conditions and record temperatures with heat indices in the 100s through the summer and into the fall of 2023' - directly identifies drought as the cause, though the declaration_id's own truncated title ('Crawfish Aquaculture Industry') doesn't state it.
Signed April 16, 2024 for the severe storms and tornadoes of April 10, 2024 named in its title.
Signed May 20, 2024 for the severe storms and tornadoes of May 14-17, 2024 named in its title. Searched around the middle of that period.
Signed June 25, 2024 for the severe storms and tornadoes of May 30 to June 4, 2024 named in its title. Searched around the middle of that period.
DOTD weight waiver dated March 10, 2021 for heavy rain and wintry precipitation from February 11, 2021 and for several days after. Searched the week starting February 11.
WAFB reported on September 14, 2004 that Governor Blanco had declared a state of emergency for Hurricane Ivan; UPI's report from the same day agrees. Dated from that coverage.
The Louisiana Register (January 2006, Vol. 32, No. 1) says the Hurricane Katrina state of emergency began Friday, August 26, 2005 under Proclamation No. 48 KBB 2005.
The Louisiana Register (October 2005, Vol. 31, No. 10) says Proclamation No. 53 KBB 2005, issued on September 20, 2005, proclaimed a state of emergency due to Hurricane Rita.

A GOHSEP release of March 2007, archived on the St. Bernard Parish mailing list, says Governor Blanco declared a state of emergency for Jefferson, Orleans and St. Martin parishes on February 13, the day after the tornadoes of February 12-13, 2007.
The Louisiana Register (September 2008, Vol. 34, No. 9) prints executive orders citing Proclamation No. 51 BJ 2008, issued August 27, 2008, for Hurricane Gustav.
The Louisiana Register (October 2008, Vol. 34, No. 10) prints an executive order citing Proclamation No. 52 BJ 2008, issued September 7, 2008, for Hurricane Ike.
KSLA printed the proclamation, signed October 30, 2009, for strong winds, heavy rain and tornadoes causing local flooding; the emergency runs from October 28, 2009.

WAFB reported the declaration on April 28, 2011 for rising Mississippi River levels. The number, Proclamation No. 41 BJ 2011, is from the Louisiana Register (June 2011, Vol. 37, No. 6, https://doa.louisiana.gov/media/mf3jcelv/1106.pdf).
NBC News (AP) reported on Friday, September 2, 2011 that the governors of Louisiana and Mississippi had declared emergencies for Tropical Storm Lee. Dated from that coverage.

The Louisiana Register (September 2012, Vol. 38, No. 9) prints executive orders citing Proclamation No. 92 BJ 2012 for Tropical Storm Isaac. FMCSA's archived copy of the declaration (via the UNT web archive) is dated Sunday, August 26, 2012.
WWNO (AP) reported on January 11, 2013 that Governor Jindal declared a statewide emergency on Thursday, January 10, 2013 after storms brought heavy rain and flooding.
The Louisiana Register (March 2014, Vol. 40, No. 3) prints an executive order citing Proclamation No. 17 BJ 2014, issued February 10, 2014, for severe winter weather.
WBRZ reported on December 30, 2015 that Governor Jindal declared a state of emergency that day ahead of flooding on the Mississippi and Red rivers.

Executive Order MJF 00-3, printed in the February 2000 Louisiana Register (page 7 of the issue PDF): after the secretary of state certified that as a result of an ice storm a state of emergency exists in the seven parishes, Governor Foster ordered that 'a state of emergency is hereby declared to exist' in them and suspended candidate qualifying there. Signed January 28, 2000.

Associated Press, June 9, 2001: Gov. Mike Foster 'declared emergencies in 11 southern parishes' after nearly 2 feet of rain from Allison that week. The story does not give the day he signed, so the row carries the date of the report; CNN reported 23 parishes with his declarations by June 11.

Associated Press, published September 24, 2002: 'Louisiana Gov. Mike Foster declared a state of emergency as a precaution' as Isidore approached. The story does not give the day he signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Associated Press story written October 1, 2002 (Lili 'entered the Gulf on Tuesday'), printed October 3: Gov. Mike Foster declared a state of emergency less than a week after Isidore. The story does not give the day he signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
